source.title: Aiming towards the minimizers: fast convergence of SGD for overparametrized problems
source.authors: Chaoyue Liu; D. Drusvyatskiy; Mikhail Belkin; Damek Davis; Yi-An Ma

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes SGD convergence for overparameterized neural networks and reports an MNIST training-loss demonstration, but it does not measure the classification-error behavior named in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give conditions and convergence guarantees for wide-network least-squares training. Figure 1 reports MNIST training loss for several batch sizes. These do not measure the classification error, shortcut, initialization comparison, stability-threshold behavior, or batch-normalization comparison specified by V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional SGD convergence for smooth, wide fully connected networks and compares MNIST training-loss curves across batch sizes. These results do not test any listed version: training classification error in convolutional networks, spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student models, depth degradation, initialization comparisons, stability-threshold dynamics, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors identify regularity conditions permitting large SGD stepsizes and iteration complexity comparable to gradient descent, and prove that these conditions hold for sufficiently wide smooth feedforward networks with linear outputs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a convergence analysis for SGD under quadratic growth and aiming conditions, then applies it to wide-network nonlinear least squares; it does not use the benchmark classification-error recipes in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical guarantee depends on network width, radius, initialization distance, stepsize, and failure probabilities. The MNIST illustration compares batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For the reported three-hidden-layer MNIST network at learning rate 0.1, the authors describe similar training-loss convergence per iteration for mini-batch SGD and full-batch GD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-batch SGD can match full-batch GD's training-loss convergence per iteration in the reported MNIST setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under stated smoothness, width, initialization, radius, and probability conditions, SGD with a constant-order stepsize converges linearly toward the zero-loss minimizer set of wide-network least-squares problems.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aiming and quadratic-growth conditions permit rapid SGD convergence for sufficiently wide smooth feedforward networks with linear outputs.

record.problems: The benchmark demonstration is MNIST training loss rather than classification error on CIFAR benchmarks. The wide-network result is a conditional theoretical guarantee, not an empirical benchmark evaluation; the MNIST figure provides no stated uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Training classification error for convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and the smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep plain tanh training, and residual training without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Large stepsizes here are not established to exceed an initial linearized stability limit. Gaussian initialization is a condition of the theorem, not an initialization comparison. Neither result warrants a verdict on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels and smaller or regularized models.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and extra student width.
Depth and identity-shortcut comparisons, including plain networks and residual networks without normalization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature dynamics, and sharpness.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: fully-connected neural network with 3 hidden layers, each of which has 1000 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Mini-batch SGD and full-batch GD trained on MNIST; constant learning rate 0.1.
rows.baseline: Full-batch GD with batch_size=60k and the same learning rate and number of iterations
rows.value: The text says mini-batch SGD has almost the same convergence behavior as full-batch GD, even for small batch sizes.
rows.note: Figure 1 includes batch sizes 64, 120, 250, 500, and 60k (full batch); the stated comparison describes mini-batch SGD generally. The plotted loss values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The reported batch-size comparison concerns training loss, which cannot establish any listed version. The qualitative value is supported by the authors' text, so evidence_form should not be figure_only. Figure 1 and its discussion appear on printed page 2.

rows.subject: fully-connected neural network with l hidden layers and a linear output layer
rows.stage_stated: randomly initialized; individual parameters initialized i.i.d. following N(0, 1)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical SGD convergence guarantee for nonlinear least-squares training.
rows.measure: Distance to the minimizer set; the corollary gives a bound after a stated number of iterations.
rows.value: With the stated probability, iterates remain in Bᵣ(w₀) and dist²(wₜ,S) ≤ ε·dist²(w₀,S) after t ≥ (1/λ₀) log(1/(εδ₂)) iterations.
rows.uncertainty: The probability bound is stated as at least 1 − p − δ₁ − δ₂ − 2 exp(−m/(2l)) − (1/m)^(Θ(ln m)).
rows.note: This is a theoretical guarantee for least-squares loss under width, radius, initialization, and probability conditions; it does not report classification error.
rows.check: This conditional theoretical distance guarantee does not measure any listed version. Correct the radius requirement to r = Ω(1/(δ₁√λ₀)), rather than Ω(1/(δ₁λ₀)). The guarantee also requires twice differentiable, Lipschitz, smooth activations and bounded inputs; it does not cover ReLU as stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
